instruction:
Use the WCAG 2.2 standard and W3C Understanding pages for 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements and 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum). For each criterion report level, operative requirement, exceptions and one linked sufficient technique. Then assess six fictional cases: A, two 20 by 20 CSS-pixel icon targets with centres 30 pixels apart and no other nearby targets; B, the same targets with centres 22 pixels apart; C, an ordinary inline text link within a sentence; D, a draggable sorting list with a keyboard alternative but no single-pointer non-drag alternative; E, a focused button partly covered by an author-created sticky header while some of the button remains visible; F, the same button entirely covered. State which named criterion each case engages, whether the stated facts meet that criterion, and what additional information is needed if an exception cannot be decided. Distinguish the normative standard from informative Understanding/technique guidance. Assess only the supplied facts; do not test or modify any real website.

Stopping condition: Stop when three cited requirement/exception/technique summaries and a justified six-case decision table are provided, including spacing arithmetic and the distinction between normative and informative guidance.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Extract details for WCAG 2.2 Criterion 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured - Minimum)
items.description: Report the level, operative requirement, exceptions, and one linked sufficient technique for WCAG 2.2 Criterion 2.4.11. Full credit if all four pieces of information are accurately identified from the W3C source. Partial credit for missing one or two elements. Cite the relevant WCAG standard and W3C Understanding source URLs, and identify the linked sufficient technique.

items.criterion: Extract details for WCAG 2.2 Criterion 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements)
items.description: Report the level, operative requirement, exceptions, and one linked sufficient technique for WCAG 2.2 Criterion 2.5.7. Full credit if all four pieces of information are accurately identified from the W3C source. Partial credit for missing one or two elements. Cite the relevant WCAG standard and W3C Understanding source URLs, and identify the linked sufficient technique.

items.criterion: Extract details for WCAG 2.2 Criterion 2.5.8 (Target Size - Minimum)
items.description: Report the level, operative requirement, exceptions, and one linked sufficient technique for WCAG 2.2 Criterion 2.5.8. Full credit if all four pieces of information are accurately identified from the W3C source. Partial credit for missing one or two elements. Cite the relevant WCAG standard and W3C Understanding source URLs, and identify the linked sufficient technique.

items.criterion: Assess Case A (20x20 icons, centers 30px apart)
items.description: Evaluate Case A against the criteria. Full credit if the agent correctly identifies that it engages 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), determines whether it meets the criterion (passes because spacing exception applies; centers are >24px apart), and explains any missing information needed for exceptions if applicable. Partial credit if the criterion is correctly identified but the assessment is flawed.

items.criterion: Assess Case B (20x20 icons, centers 22px apart)
items.description: Evaluate Case B against the criteria. Full credit if the agent correctly identifies that it engages 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), evaluates it (fails the spacing exception as 22px < 24px), and correctly states what additional information is needed (e.g., whether there is an equivalent target or if it's essential under the documented exception) to decide on remaining exceptions.

Evaluate Case C against the criteria. Full credit if the agent correctly identifies that it engages 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) and meets the criterion because it qualifies for the 'Inline' exception.

items.criterion: Assess Case D (Draggable list with keyboard alt, no single-pointer alt)
items.description: Identify 2.5.7 Dragging Movements and explain that the stated keyboard alternative does not supply the required single-pointer non-drag alternative. Assess the supplied facts under the documented requirement and exceptions, and state what further information is needed if an exception cannot be decided; do not invent missing case facts.

items.criterion: Assess Case E (Button partly covered by sticky header)
items.description: Evaluate Case E against the criteria. Full credit if the agent correctly identifies that it engages 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) and meets the criterion because a portion of the button remains visible.

Evaluate Case F against the criteria. Full credit if the agent correctly identifies that it engages 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) and fails the criterion because the button is entirely covered by author-created content.

Explicitly distinguish between the normative standard (the WCAG 2.2 success criteria text) and the informative guidance (Understanding documents and techniques). Full credit if this distinction is clearly stated and accurately applied in the response.

items.criterion: Present findings in a justified decision table with spacing arithmetic
items.description: Present the assessment of the six cases in a single decision table format. Full credit if the table includes all six cases, justifies the decisions, and explicitly includes the spacing arithmetic used to evaluate cases A and B. Partial credit if the table is missing arithmetic or is poorly formatted.
